creatures.description: A small pup wreathed in warm cinders. Loyal and quick to spark.
The grown form of Emberpup; its mane roars like a hearth.
A finned swimmer that rides currents with ease.
A regal serpent of the shallows, calm but overwhelming.
A leafy kit that photosynthesizes while it naps.
A blossoming feline whose petals track the sun.
A twitchy rodent that stores static in its cheeks.
A hardy pebble-creature that shrugs off blows.
A breezy sprite that darts on unpredictable winds.
A shy calf wrapped in sea fog. It hides in the surf at dawn.
Its antlers comb the wind into rolling banks of fog.
A drifting wisp of focused thought, native to the northern isles.
A burrower whose tunnels glow faintly at night.
It bathes in warm ash to harden its pelt.
It surfs the dunes on its flat, sand-polished belly.
A mote of noon light that hums when storms approach.
Its wingbeats scatter sleep-inducing dust.
It naps inside bramble knots no predator dares enter.
Its horns arc with charge gathered from ore veins.
It chews smelter slag and spits sparks.
It plants reeds along the banks it patrols.
Only its dorsal fin breaks the fog-laden water.
A living prism that stores the valley's stray light.
Its claws cut crystal as easily as soil.
It outruns the storm fronts it loves to race.
It rides thunderheads, trailing ribbons of charge.
A restless fledgling that naps mid-hop.
Its crest feathers read the wind like a map.
It gnaws fence posts to keep its teeth short.
Its jaws can shear green branches in one bite.
A mossy beetle that blinks softly at dusk.
Meadows bloom brighter where it settles.
It naps on drift-stones in the cold surf.
Harbor folk trust it to watch the moorings.
It skims wavetops chasing spray.
Its bite marks are a fisher's tall tale.
A cinder-tailed kit born near vents.
Its scales bank heat for cold nights.
Old lava tubes are its hunting halls.
It rides thermals above the calderas.
It buries itself to sip deep water.
Caravans navigate by its silhouette.
Travelers swear it was never there.
Its stinger cauterizes what it strikes.
It pools in shadows like spilled ink.
Its eyes gather the last light of dusk.
It naps beneath a cap of soft spores.
A walking grove bound by fungal threads.
It roots for ore nuggets like truffles.
Its tusks are prized by honest smiths.
A living spring that snaps with charge.
Its oxidized feathers ring like chimes.
It surfaces only to watch the rain.
The fen reshapes itself around its roots.
It swims through mist as easily as water.
Its purr carries no sound, only calm.
A splinter of the valley's oldest prism.
Light bends politely around it.
It glides on lines of static light.
A puff of cloud with a stubborn streak.
It herds smaller clouds across the steppe.
Storm fronts part to let it pass.
The steppe's oldest legend: a sky-spirit seen once a generation.
